column1: # Written by Claude (origin "claude"). One line per entry:  entry id|typical learner mistake|usage note
# Notes are in English. Either text column may be empty.

fr:être:verb|Some verbs make the passé composé with être, not avoir: aller, venir, arriver, partir, naître, mourir, rester, tomber … and every reflexive verb: "je suis allé", "je me suis levé".|With être the past participle agrees with the subject: "elle est allée", "ils sont venus".
fr:avoir:verb|Age uses avoir: "j'ai vingt ans", not "je suis vingt". Also avoir faim, avoir soif, avoir froid, avoir peur.|
fr:aller:verb||Aller + infinitive is the near future: "je vais manger" (I'm going to eat).
fr:faire:verb||Weather uses faire: "il fait beau", "il fait froid".
fr:savoir:verb|Savoir is for facts and skills ("je sais nager"), connaître for people and places ("je connais Paris").|
fr:connaître:verb|Connaître is for people, places and things you are familiar with; for facts and skills use savoir: "je sais où il habite".|
fr:pouvoir:verb|For a learned skill French uses savoir: "je sais nager" (I can swim). "Je peux nager" means I'm able to or allowed to right now.|
fr:attendre:verb|Attendre means to wait (for): "j'attends le bus". To attend is "assister à".|
fr:assister:verb|"Assister à" means to attend (a class, a concert). To help is aider.|
fr:rester:verb|Rester means to stay, not to rest (se reposer). It takes être: "je suis resté".|
fr:actuellement:adverb|Means currently, not actually. "Actually" is "en fait".|
fr:librairie:noun|A librairie is a bookshop. A library is "une bibliothèque".|
fr:monnaie:noun|Monnaie is change (coins) or a currency. Money in general is "l'argent".|
fr:argent:noun||Argent means both money and silver.
fr:gens:noun|Gens is always plural: "les gens sont gentils". For one person say "une personne".|
fr:personne:pronoun|With ne, personne means nobody: "je ne vois personne". As a noun, "une personne" is a person.|
fr:on:pronoun||In everyday speech on means "we": "on y va?" It also means "one, people" in general. The verb is always third person singular: "on est", "on va".
fr:tu:pronoun||Tu for friends, family and children; vous for strangers, older people, at work, and for more than one person.
fr:vous:pronoun||Vous is the polite "you" for one person and the normal "you" for several people.
fr:déception:noun|Déception means disappointment, not deception (tromperie).|
fr:sensible:adjective|Sensible means sensitive. "Sensible" in English is "raisonnable".|
fr:sympathique:adjective|Means nice, friendly. Sympathetic (showing pity) is "compatissant".|
fr:large:adjective|Large means wide. Big is grand.|
fr:location:noun|Location means renting or a rental. A location (place) is "un endroit" or "un lieu".|
fr:coin:noun|Coin means corner. A coin (money) is "une pièce".|
fr:passer:verb|"Passer un examen" means to take an exam. To pass it is "réussir un examen".|
fr:demander:verb|Demander means to ask, not to demand (exiger).|
fr:visiter:verb|Visiter is for places. For people use "rendre visite à": "je rends visite à ma grand-mère".|
fr:chez:preposition||Chez + a person means at or to their home or business: "chez moi", "chez le médecin".
fr:depuis:preposition|For something still going on, depuis takes the present tense: "j'habite ici depuis deux ans" (I have lived here for two years).|
fr:bon:adjective|Bon is the adjective (good), bien the adverb (well): "un bon livre", "il chante bien". But "c'est bien" (that's good).|
fr:bien:adverb|Bien is the adverb (well), bon the adjective (good): "il parle bien", "un bon repas".|
fr:beau:adjective||Before a masculine noun starting with a vowel sound it becomes bel: "un bel homme". The same with nouveau → nouvel and vieux → vieil.
fr:très:adverb|Never "très beaucoup": "merci beaucoup", "j'aime beaucoup".|
fr:beaucoup:adverb||Beaucoup de + noun, with no article: "beaucoup de livres", "beaucoup d'eau".
fr:collège:noun|In France the collège is the school for ages 11 to 15. A college or university is "une université" or "une école".|
fr:éventuellement:adverb|Means possibly, if need be, not eventually. Eventually is "finalement" or "à la fin".|
fr:préservatif:noun|Means condom. A preservative is "un conservateur".|
fr:excité:adjective|Often means agitated or sexually aroused. To say you are excited about something: "j'ai hâte" or "je suis enthousiaste".|
fr:chance:noun|Chance means luck: "bonne chance!" A chance in the sense of an opportunity is often "une occasion".|
fr:habiter:verb||Habiter can be used with or without à: "j'habite (à) Zurich".
fr:quitter:verb|Quitter needs an object: "je quitte la maison". On its own, "to leave" is partir: "je pars".|
fr:entendre:verb|Entendre means to hear. To understand is comprendre (entendre in this sense is old-fashioned).|
fr:blesser:verb|Blesser means to injure or hurt, not to bless (bénir).|
